testing_note: Author walkthrough only, no separate agent run: wrote scratch/case1.md (customer claims P1 and a sales-rep credit promise, support reproduces only a partial failure, an internal note approves a credit, a timed update promise, a policy silent on time zone) and walked the skill through it, plus a policy-missing partial-input case and a thread-missing case. Changes made: internal notes of approved-but-uncommunicated promises are now listed separately rather than as commitments; the priority check now uses verified evidence and handles custom service levels whose terms are not supplied; attempts without a recorded result say 'result not recorded'.
applied_note: I started from reader and purpose (a next-tier engineer picking up the case cold) and assigned each input as the single authority for its part of the handoff, with a missing-input branch for each that finishes the remaining sections and lists what is blocked, and a supplied-material rule placed beside the authority table. Completion is bounded by an output template with size limits and a short observable final check; the Reported/Verified and commitment definitions are co-located with their rules and exceptions. Everything every run needs is inline in one SKILL.md with a model-invoked description holding one trigger branch, so no extra files were added.
model: claude-opus-5-5 (inherited by a fresh general-purpose subagent)
